# Standing decisions

**Status**: normative. A deviation is raised in a design plan, not improvised.

## 2. Standing decisions

Three decisions are already made and shape everything that follows.

### 2.1 Feature parity with a new API

The core is designed on its own terms rather than shaped to fit cornerstone's. The cost lands squarely on the existing product: a new API means a migration, and it is a first-class epic (E17, twenty engineer-weeks), not a cleanup task. §12 is the strategy.

### 2.2 The core stays WebAssembly-agnostic

wasm-bindgen appears in exactly one crate. This is what makes Phases 2 and 3 possible without a rewrite. It is nearly free to hold and expensive to restore, so it is a CI check from day one — see §15.3.

### 2.3 Validation is infrastructure, not a phase

Cornerstone3D is a working reference oracle. The differential harness is built before any port code. Given agent-assisted delivery, it is the mechanism that makes generated Rust safe to merge at volume; without it, generation speed is a liability rather than an advantage.
